neighbours.label: The punctuation mark (dash, colon, ellipsis, question mark) placed right after a joining word such as but, and, so, or, then, yet or because, in any language, before the sentence carries on; weaker after a sentence adverb (still, sadly) or with a plain comma after the joining word. Quiet: the same dashes and colons after ordinary nouns or verbs (asides, list intros), and commas after openers like 'However,'.
neighbours.short: punctuation right after a joining word (But –, So:)
fire: I wanted to call her back, but — honestly — I lost my nerve.
We packed the car and... we just sat there staring at the rain.
He studied all night, so: the exam went better than expected.
You can stay here or — if you prefer — take the late train home.
She opened the letter, then... she started to laugh.
The bridge looked solid, yet — as we soon learned — it was rotting underneath.
I left early because... well, the meeting had become pointless.
Quería ir a la fiesta, pero... al final me quedé en casa.
quiet: I wanted to call her back — honestly a hard decision — and I did it the next day.
We packed three things: a tent, a stove and two sleeping bags.
He studied all night for the exam, which went better than expected.
You can stay here tonight if you prefer to skip the late train home.
She opened the letter... from her grandmother, sent forty years ago.
The bridge — built in 1890 — was rotting underneath.
However, the meeting had become pointless by noon.
Quería ir a la fiesta: música, amigos y comida.
